title: Collect Collodarian Nuclei for Genomic Analyses
author: Estelle Bigeard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5kgg4tw

steps.title: Prepare 3 M sucrose stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 112.96 g sucrose, dissolve in 110 mL Milli‑Q water, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M spermine
steps.instruction: Weigh 40.5 mg spermine free base into a 15 mL Falcon tube, add 2 mL Milli‑Q water, mix until clear (solubility 50 mg mL⁻¹); store at 2–8 °C in degassed water, aliquot frozen under argon or nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare 0.05 M spermidine
steps.instruction: Weigh 87.15 mg spermidine into a 15 mL Falcon tube, add 12 mL Milli‑Q water, mix (soluble 50 mg mL⁻¹); filter through a 0.22 µm filter, store single‑use aliquots at –20 °C (max 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare 4 M NaCl stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.47 g NaCl, dissolve in 2 mL Milli‑Q water, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 5 M KCl stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 2.6 g KCl, dissolve in 7 mL Milli‑Q water, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M EDTA pH 8
steps.instruction: Weigh 15 g EDTA, add 50 mL Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 8 with NaOH pellets, bring volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.2 µm filter, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8
steps.instruction: Weigh 15.76 g Tris‑HCl, dissolve in Milli‑Q water and make up to 100 mL, adjust pH to 8, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Make 500 mL Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine the following into a container and bring to 500 mL with Milli‑Q water: 50 mL 3 M sucrose (final 0.3 M), 6 mL 5 M KCl (final 60 mM), 1.875 mL 4 M NaCl (final 15 mM), 30 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8 (final 60 mM), 5 mL 0.05 M spermidine (final 0.5 mM), 750 µL 0.1 M spermine (final 0.15 mM), 2 mL 0.5 M EDTA (final 2 mM), 2.5 mL Igepal CA‑630; mix well.

steps.title: Sort colonies by morphology
steps.instruction: Select up to 20 colonies representing distinct morphological types (segmented round, segmented straight, non‑segmented, purple, blue‑dot, etc.), observe under a stereomicroscope, and photograph both wide‑field and zoomed views.

steps.title: Perform first lysis
steps.instruction: In a 6‑well plate add 8 mL Lysis solution to each well; place a 40 µm diameter sieve (pre‑rinsed with Milli‑Q water) into each well; add ~10 medium‑sized colonies (1.5–2 cm) onto each sieve; incubate 30 min at room temperature; then transfer each sieve to a 90 mm petri dish containing fresh Lysis solution, tap and shake the sieve for ~3 min until the matrix disintegrates and releases nuclei.

steps.title: Perform second lysis (if needed)
steps.instruction: For colonies that are not purple or blue‑dot, repeat the lysis: add 8 mL fresh Lysis solution to a new 6‑well plate, place the previously lysed sieve at the start, and incubate another 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash nuclei in buffer
steps.instruction: Remove each sieve from the lysis well, place it into a petri dish containing Wash Buffer, tap and shake the sieve repeatedly until the matrix is completely removed; inspect with a binocular loupe, and photograph the cleaned sample.

steps.title: Rinse capsules and collect
steps.instruction: Rinse the released capsules in 1× PBS or 0.2 µm‑filtered, autoclaved seawater within a 90 mm petri dish; transfer capsules from the sieve by rinsing with the same solution into a 1.5 mL (or 2 mL if needed) microtube; centrifuge at 1000 rcf for 10 min; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze and store
steps.instruction: Place the microtube in a flash freezer, then store at –80 °C.

steps.title: PBS rinse before DNA extraction
steps.instruction: If seawater was used, add 500 µL 1× PBS to the microtube, tap gently, centrifuge 1000 rcf for 10 min, remove supernatant; repeat once if necessary.

steps.title: Proceed to DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Follow the separate DNA extraction protocol (published on protocols.io in collaboration with Genoscope).
